newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean court upholds life term for ex-president.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean court upholds life term for ex-president.

text.p: South Korea's Supreme Court on Thursday upheld a sentence of life in jail for former president Chun Doo Hwan for mutiny, treason and bribery, court officials said.
The court also confirmed a 17-year jail sentence for his successor Roh Tae-woo for similar convictions.
Prosecutors had challenged as too lenient an appeal court decision last December to commute Chun's death sentence to life in jail and to cut Roh's prison term from 22-1/2 years to 17.

Chun and Roh were found guilty of mutiny and treason in connection with a 1979 coup that launched Chun's rise to power and a 1980 massacre of pro-democracy activists in the southwestern city of Kwangju.
The disgraced former heads of state were also convicted of corruption after amassing huge slush funds. Chun was president from 1980-1988 and Roh succeeded him, stepping down in 1993.
The Supreme Court is South Korea's court of final appeal.
